ai_readiness.method: Each dimension starts at 100 and loses severity_penalty x (0.4 + 0.6 x reach) x confidence for every finding attributed to it. The overall score is the weighted mean of the applicable dimensions.

findings.title: robots.txt blocks 15 named AI or answer-engine crawler(s) from the entire site
findings.evidence: robots.txt contains a 'Disallow: /' group for: gptbot (OpenAI (training and retrieval)); oai-searchbot (OpenAI search); chatgpt-user (ChatGPT user-initiated fetch); claudebot (Anthropic); claude-user (Claude user-initiated fetch); claude-searchbot (Claude search); perplexitybot (Perplexity); perplexity-user (Perplexity user-initiated fetch). General crawling is not blocked, so these agents are singled out. Read from the per-user-agent groups in robots.txt. Agents that merely fall back to the '*' group are not counted here.

suggested_action.summary: Confirm whether this block is a deliberate content policy; if AI visibility is the goal, allow the agents you want to be discovered by.
steps: Decide per agent whether the goal is content protection or AI visibility - these pull in opposite directions.
For agents you want to be discoverable in, remove the 'Disallow: /' from their group or narrow it to private paths.
Keep training-only agents blocked separately from retrieval agents if you want citation without training use.
Re-check robots.txt after deployment with each agent token.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation; single-page sample; consistent across 1/1 pages
findings.impact: These are the crawlers that assistants and answer engines use to reach a site. While they are disallowed, the brand cannot be retrieved, quoted or cited by those systems no matter how good the on-page content is - third-party descriptions are used instead.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.80 (severity high) x reach 1.00 x confidence 0.82 x fixability 1.00

General crawling is not blocked, so these agents are singled out.
technical_details.details: Read from the per-user-agent groups in robots.txt. Agents that merely fall back to the '*' group are not counted here.

possible_benign_explanations: Blocking these agents is often a deliberate content-licensing or copyright decision, in which case this is working as intended and should be recorded as accepted rather than fixed.
Some organisations block training crawlers while allowing retrieval crawlers; check the finding's agent list before acting.

findings.title: 2 likely-important page(s) have no H1 heading
findings.evidence: https://www.amazon.com/ has no <h1> (40 headings of any level); https://www.amazon.com/haul/store?ref_=nav_cs_hul_disb has no <h1> (2 headings of any level)

suggested_action.summary: Give each of these pages one descriptive H1 that names its subject.
steps: Add a single <h1> stating what the page is about.
Keep the heading hierarchy ordered (h1 then h2 then h3).
Avoid using an image of text as the page heading.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation
findings.impact: Without a top-level heading the page's subject has to be inferred from the title alone, which weakens topical understanding.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.50 (severity medium) x reach 0.67 x confidence 0.85 x fixability 0.95

technical_details.observation: https://www.amazon.com/ has no <h1> (40 headings of any level); https://www.amazon.com/haul/store?ref_=nav_cs_hul_disb has no <h1> (2 headings of any level)

findings.title: No XML sitemap was found
findings.evidence: Neither /sitemap.xml nor any Sitemap: directive in robots.txt returned a usable sitemap. 7 HTML pages were reachable by link following.

suggested_action.summary: Publish an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt.
steps: Generate a sitemap listing canonical URLs of the public pages.
Serve it at /sitemap.xml with HTTP 200 and content-type application/xml.
Add a 'Sitemap: https://<host>/sitemap.xml' line to robots.txt.

findings.confidence_reason: deterministic rule on measured values; direct DOM/HTTP observation; sample of 7 pages
findings.impact: Without a sitemap, automated systems must rely entirely on link discovery, so pages that are weakly linked may never be reached.
findings.priority_reason: impact 0.50 (severity medium) x reach 0.50 x confidence 0.90 x fixability 0.90
